Hernia Symptoms Progression

Herecomesdoc, CC BY-SA 3.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0>, via Wikimedia Commons · https://www.myupchar.com/en, CC BY-SA 4.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0>, via Wikimedia Commons

1. First symptom of hernia

Hernia start as a visible bulge that can be seen only when coughing or straining and it goes back to normal afterwards

AfroBrazilian, CC BY-SA 3.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
BruceBlaus, CC BY-SA 4.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0>, via Wikimedia Commons

Hernia contents

Intestine

Omentum

Fallopian tube or uterus in women

Stomach

Saltanat ebli, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons

2. First progression of hernia

Bulge become more visible and it has to be pushed back to get reduced (reducible)

Pressure at the affected area

Strenerkou, CC BY-SA 4.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0>, via Wikimedia Commons

3. Second progression of hernia

The visible bulge can’t be reduced back anymore (irreducible or incarcerated)

Pain or discomfort at the area

It might be associated with bowel obstruction (gives symptoms like nausea and vomiting)

Treatment with surgery is urgent

Svenscar69, CC BY-SA 4.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0>, via Wikimedia Commons

4. Third progression of hernia

irreducible hernia become strangulated (blood supply to the hernia content become compromised)

Onset of burning or sharp pain

Swelling

Nausea and vomiting, constipation

James Heilman, MD, CC BY-SA 4.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0>, via Wikimedia Commons

4. Fourth progression of hernia

Fever

Treatment with surgery is emergent (it has to be done right now)

If not treated then the content of the hernia become infarcted and die and this lead to peritonitis

Milliways, CC BY-SA 3.0 <http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/>, via Wikimedia Commons
Anpol42, CC BY-SA 3.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0>, via Wikimedia Commons · U.S. Navy photo, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
